data.plain: Giving doctrine prose the authority of an executable rule before it passes the grammar and lists the result records it must produce.

analogy.boundary: The picture only covers notes that were never registered; a registered pass can still be wrong.

maps.analogy: the handwritten note on the door
maps.doctrine: the written doctrine claiming to govern

maps.analogy: being registered in the building's access system
maps.doctrine: being accepted by the executable grammar

maps.analogy: saying what evidence of access has to be shown
maps.doctrine: the record obligations it has to declare

maps.analogy: naming the rooms and hours the pass leaves out
maps.doctrine: the stated limits of its scope

analogy.text: Treating a handwritten note taped to a door, saying 'this person may enter', as real access, although it was never entered into the building's access system and never says which rooms or hours it covers.

reader.counterexample: A confidently worded policy paragraph is cited as the rule for some behaviour, although nothing parses or checks it and it never says what it leaves out.
reader.does_not_prove: A standard that passes the grammar is still only as strong as the obligations it carries.

example.text: The executable doctrine grammar accepts a standard as binding only when it parses and carries its obligation and scope-limit fields, and its tests include a written-only standard that claims to be complete, which the grammar rejects.

reader.governs: The line between rules that are enforced and text that only reads like a rule.
reader.plain: The mistake of treating a confidently written paragraph as a binding rule when it never went through the system's formal checks and never says what evidence it owes or where it applies.
reader.potential_misread: That a clearly and firmly worded statement is a rule the system enforces because of how it reads.
reader.refuses: Giving binding force to written doctrine that the grammar has not accepted and that declares no record obligations or scope limits.
reader.requires: Grammar acceptance plus declared record obligations and scope limits before a piece of doctrine counts as binding.
reader.why_it_matters: It keeps confident paragraphs from piling up and being treated as enforced rules that nothing can check.
